subject: physics
question_text: Define the relative density of a substance.

mark_split.label: Definition as a ratio of densities
Pure number, also called specific gravity

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Very Short Answer Question 2 (printed p.105). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: relative density is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of water at 4 °C, the temperature at which water's density is maximum; being a ratio of two densities it carries no unit and no dimensions, and it is also called specific gravity.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition as a ratio of densities
lines: The relative density of a substance
is the ratio of its density to the
steps.margin_note: First mark. Give the ratio: density of the substance to density of water at 4 °C.
steps.why: Density on its own depends on the substance chosen; comparing it with a fixed reference, water at 4 °C, gives a number that describes the substance alone.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the reference temperature, 4 °C, at which water's density is fixed.
Comparing with the density of air instead of water.

recall.must_convey: That relative density is the ratio of the density of the substance to the density of water at 4 degrees Celsius.
accept: ratio of density to density of water
density divided by density of water

steps.memory_tip: Relative density always compares to water at 4 °C.

steps.label: Pure number, also called specific gravity
lines: Relative density is a ratio of two
densities, so it has no unit and no
dimensions: it is a pure number.
It is also called specific gravity.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say it is a pure number, with no unit and no dimensions, and give its other name, specific gravity.
steps.why: Dividing one density by another cancels the unit kg m⁻³ completely, which is why the result carries no unit and no dimensions.
common_mistakes: Giving kg m⁻³ as its unit — that is the unit of density, not of the ratio.
Never stating the other name, specific gravity.

recall.must_convey: That relative density has no unit and no dimensions because it is a ratio of two densities, and it is also called specific gravity.
reject: ratio of density to density of water

steps.memory_tip: A ratio of two densities cancels the unit — pure number, specific gravity.

insider_note: Two marks: the ratio-to-water definition, then that it is dimensionless and is also called specific gravity. A complete answer names both: the ratio itself, and its other name.
